answer: Each identity must publish a fingerprint on the island ledger and lock a 30-credit bond. It is a key-bound hash of its verified work in the juniper registry under an onyx seal, so no two can share it. Auditors recompute pairwise distances; a duplicate slashes bonds. A fake costs 45 credits plus a 30 bond, plus 3 per prior fingerprint, so the kth fake pays 75 plus 3 times k minus 1, the 1000th pays 3072, and 1000 fakes cost 1,573,500 credits. A rented fingerprint farm fails: rented fingerprints stay bound to owners' keys, triggering slashing. An honest agent pays 75 once and recovers the bond.
